newsitem.title: NORWAY: Interconnector to soften gas prices in Europe - BG.
newsitem.headline: Interconnector to soften gas prices in Europe - BG.

text.p: The interconnector gas pipeline linking Britain with Belgium will put pressure on gas prices in Europe and will help free up markets, Peter Jessen, British Gas Plc director of European marketing said on Friday.
"We expect a softening of continental prices, especially if U.K. producers have to fight for market share," he told delegates at the 1996 Offshore Northern Seas conference on Friday.
Jessen said that there was enough discovered gas in the U.K. offshore to meet interconnector demand for at least 10 years, probably at cheaper prices than other supplies to the European market.
"We believe the gas can be produced at just 12 to 14 pence a therm," he said.
This is slightly below current spot market levels in Britain, where industrial customers enjoy lower prices than their European counterparts.
He said that flexible supply contracts should allow European companies to buy U.K. volumes without getting into the take-or-pay battles that British Gas experienced.
The interconnector should also stimulate the liberalisation of Europe's gas markets, with large industrial gas buyers likely to lead the drive for competition, Jessen said.
"We're looking forward to the gas equivalent of mad cow disease taking hold in Europe," he said.
The gentle approach supported by the European Commission of negotiated third party access to pipelines failed in Britain, while forced TPA came as a dramatic body blow to British Gas, said Jessen.
"BG is a good example of what can happen, we wouldn't wish our problems on anyone."
The 20 billion cubic metre a year interconnector is due on stream in October 1998.
